name: a derived reciprocal never auto-overwrites a primary fact
description: Celine already has a PRIMARY spouse edge (-> Aldo) from her own note. A later note 'Jeff married Celine' would reflect a derived Celine.spouse -> Jeff, which on the functional key would supersede the primary. The derived-defers-to-primary rule forbids that (docs/research/fix-options/2): the primary stays active and the reflection parks in pending_review, reported on the result line of the fact whose reciprocal was refused — the reflection is a row the model never named, so it has no result line of its own. ONE CHANNEL (AGENT_INGEST_REWRITE R1b): the harness IS the note conversation, and a conversation's write path no longer files a review card — `decide()` reports the hold back in the tool result and the AGENT settles it, by re-reading the note or by asking the owner. So the count is 0 and the ROW STATUSES above are the whole assertion, which is exactly the point: `decide()`'s authority over what LANDS is untouched, only who is told moved.
